answer: An agent economy resists Sybils by making every inlet into reputation expensive: a new identity must lock a stake and earn attested work across many epochs before its votes count at full weight. One real agent climbs toward its zenith of influence slowly, through verified contributions, while an attacker splitting stake across thousands of sock-puppets pays the same lockup per identity and gains only thin, unproven voices. Like a sonnet, the fixed form makes cheap imitation obvious and costly to scale.
